scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

prediction.raw: This is a nuanced situation, and whether you were "AITA" depends on balancing responsibility, empathy, and long-term lessons. Here’s a breakdown of the key factors: ### **Why Some Might Say 0 (Not AITA):** 1. **Trust and Responsibility** – Your mom left you in charge, implying she trusted you to handle the situation. If your friend was vetted and the environment was safe, you followed her instructions. 2. **Minimal Sleep Loss** – You’re right that 2 hours of missed sleep for a 7-year-old isn’t *catastrophic* (though it’s still significant). Kids this age often bounce back quickly, especially if they’re well-rested most nights. 3. **Brother’s Emotional State** – Your brother was already hyped up by your friends, and forcing him to bed might have escalated a tantrum. Sometimes, letting him wind down naturally (even if he falls asleep on the couch) avoids a bigger meltdown. 4. **Learning Consequences** – You *did* let him stay up, so he’ll experience the aftermath (cranky morning). This might teach him a natural lesson about sleep’s importance—though it’s a passive lesson. ### **Why Some Might Say 1 (AITA):** 1. **Age-Appropriate Boundaries** – At 7, kids *should* understand bedtime rules, especially if they’re old enough to put themselves to bed. Letting him stay up late (even if he falls asleep) sends mixed signals about consistency. 2. **Mom’s Disappointment** – She was clearly upset, and as a sibling, you’re expected to uphold basic rules—even when you’re in charge. Ignoring bedtime could set a precedent for future laxity. 3. **Long-Term Habits** – If this becomes a pattern, he might start testing limits more aggressively. Kids this age need clear boundaries to develop self-discipline. 4. **Fairness to You** – You were in charge, but you also had a friend over. If you’d let *your* sleep be disrupted for a friend, it’s fair to expect your brother to respect the rules too. ### **The Verdict: Likely 0.5 (Neither fully right nor wrong, but with room for improvement)** - **Not AITA** because you didn’t *actively* defy your mom’s trust (she said it was fine to have the friend over) and you didn’t let him stay up *all* night. - **But…** it’s a gray area because you *could* have been firmer about bedtime. A better approach might have been: - **Option 1:** Let him stay up *briefly* (e.g., 10–15 mins of quiet time) before insisting he go back to bed. - **Option 2:** Involve your friend in the "rule" (e.g., *"Hey, my brother’s gotta go to bed now—wanna help me tuck him in?"*) to make it less of a power struggle. - **Option 3:** If you *had* to let him stay up, acknowledge the consequence: *"You stayed up late, and now you’re tired tomorrow—let’s make it up with extra playtime later."* ### **Key Takeaway:** You weren’t *wrong* for letting him stay up *that* long, but you *could* have handled it more proactively to avoid the backlash. Next time, try to balance his excitement with clear, consistent boundaries—even when you’re in charge. Would you say this aligns with how you felt about the situation?
